newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Asian immigration beneficial to NZ economy - study.
newsitem.headline: Asian immigration beneficial to NZ economy - study.

text.p: Immigration to New Zealand is economically beneficial, not detrimental, according to a new study published by Enterprise Auckland on Wednesday.
Recent Asian immigrants have increased economic output in the Auckland region by $22 million per year, and all over New Zealand by $28 million per year, it said.
The survey talked to members of the five major ethnic groups which represent two-thirds of recent migration to New Zealand: China, Hong Kong, Japan, South Korea and Taiwan.

It showed that these immigrants were not taking away jobs from New Zealanders. Two thirds have their own business, one third having bought an existing business, the other third have started their own and therefore created new jobs for other New Zealanders.
Enterprise Auckland ran the survey on behalf of Auckland Institute of Studies (AIS) in order to examine the economic impact of immigration.
A conclusion from the study was that the criticism of Asian immigrants to New Zealand was based on ignorance rather than fact.

Michael Barnett, chief executive of the Auckland Regional Chamber of Commerce and Industry, said: "We must concentrate on the qualities Asian migrants are bringing to New Zealand...rather than their country of origin."
